summary: Request: Scoped temporary proxy role to perform cross-cloud production debugging without bastion accounts
description:
Issue summary:
Requesting a short-lived, tightly-scoped proxy role that allows SRE engineers to perform interactive debugging and log collection across both AWS and GCP production accounts without provisioning long-lived bastion accounts.

Impact / Motivation:
- Current incident debugging requires spinning up jump VMs or handing out broad cross-account roles which increases blast radius and audit noise.
- We need ephemeral access for a 48-hour window to triage a recurring downstream latency spike observed in prod-us-east and prod-eu-west.

Access requested (concrete):
- AWS: A cross-account role in the infra-managed monitoring account that can be assumed via STS:AssumeRole with session duration capped at 1 hour and forced MFA. Allowed actions limited to: logs:DescribeLogGroups, logs:GetLogEvents, logs:FilterLogEvents, ec2:DescribeInstances, ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces, ssm:StartSession (only on instances tagged debug=true), kms:Decrypt (for one specific KMS key id).
- GCP: A short-lived service account impersonation pathway (workload identity) that grants logging.viewer, compute.instances.get, compute.instances.list and iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for the debug-proxy SA only. Token TTL capped at 60 minutes.
- Central proxy: A small ephemeral bastionless proxy container in an ops project that performs request forwarding; role must allow only port-forwarding with no persistent shell access.

Duration and scope:
- Requested window: 2026-03-15 09:00 -> 2026-03-17 09:00 UTC (48h).
- Access must be scoped to resources with tag "team:sre" or projects listed: prod-us-east, prod-eu-west, staging-us-west.

Controls required by Security:
- All assume/impersonation events must be exported to Cloud Audit Logs / CloudTrail and forwarded to Splunk with a dedicated tag debug-session=INT-912345.
- Session recordings for any SSM sessions and gcloud sessions stored for 90 days.
- Automated revoke after 60 minutes of inactivity.
- Approval must come from oncall-sre and security:security-eng prior to enabling.

Justification and approvers:
- Primary justification: urgent reproduction of intermittent KV cache evictions that correlate with latency spikes.
- Approvers requested: Priya Nand (oncall-sre), Marcus Feld (security-eng), Diego Martinez (infra).

Work to be done by Infra team if approved:
- Create IAM role in AWS with a restrictive trust policy targeted to OIDC connector and MFA validation.
- Create a GCP IAM binding and service account with workload identity pool mapping and short TTL.
- Provision a proxy container image and a deployment manifest limited to ops namespace with NetworkPolicy restricting egress only to necessary endpoints.
- Document the exact principals and commands to assume the role in the runbook page linked above.

Acceptance criteria:
- SRE can assume the cross-cloud proxy role via documented CLI steps and obtain audit-tagged credentials that expire automatically.
- CloudTrail / Cloud Audit Logs show assume/impersonation events with INT-912345 tag.
- No broader IAM privileges exist beyond the ones enumerated.

Notes on urgency: This is timeboxed access for an active debugging window. If not granted before 2026-03-15 08:00 UTC, the SRE team will fallback to the existing jump-host process (higher blast radius).

investigation_notes:
Initial checks performed:
- Correlated latency spikes with backend KV eviction metrics in Datadog (spikes at 02:40 and 11:15 UTC last three days).
- Verified that current jump-host workflow requires full ec2:StartInstances and broad IAM role assumptions which is more permissive than this request.
- Confirmed existing CloudTrail capture and Splunk ingestion are functioning for prod accounts.
- Ran a dry-run assume-role test with a staging role to validate TTL enforcement and MFA challenge flows. Results: TTL enforced, MFA trigger working.
resolution: Pending completion of infra PR and security checklist. Infra to notify ticket when proxy image is deployed to ops namespace and when CloudTrail/Splunk tagging is validated. After validation, access will be enabled and SRE will confirm ability to perform required debug steps.
